"Function: Regulatory and secretory organ. TSH is the primary messenger that leads to T3 and T4 production. TH  regulates Thermogenesis, energy utilization by increasing the basal metabolic rate and regulate lipid and glucose metabolism.
- Hyperthyroid condition: Increased heart rate, increased metabolism, can lead to high blood glucose levels due to high liver glucose production.
- Hypothyroidism: Reduced metabolism, higher cholesterol and triglycerides in blood, higher blood pressure.
--> Bidirectional link between TH and adiposity: 
A) TH promotes fat storage + lowers energy expenditure
B) Excess fat tissue releases inflammatory cytokines and leptin which alters TSH secretion. They have elevates TSH levels with a healthy thyroid.
Metabolism:
- Hormone production.
- TSH influences the enzyme that turns inactive T4 into active T4.
Key Metabolites: 
Key Proteins: TH (T3 and T4), TSH (Thyrotropin)
Sources:
- doi: 10.1177/2042018820917869
- https://doi.org/10.1152/physrev.00030.2013
"

"Function: Energy storage. 
Metabolism: Lipolysis during fasting. 
Key Metabolites: Secretes Leptin, which regulates hunger. Secretes lipolysis products: free fatty acids, glycerol. Insulin resistance: 
- WAT and Muscle are impaired in taking up glucose while the liver looses its ability in endogenous glucose production. Leads to the uncontrolled release of fatty acids from the WAT.
- "A current view, which proposes adipocyte dysfunction as an early cardinal event in insulin resistance, is that WAT drives metabolic fluxes that affect the liver and skeletal muscle"[Morigny et. al.], [Roden et. al.]
- The pancreas beta-cells have an increased burden to produce insulin. The function may then decline with time. Correlation is present in low-BMI (non diabetic?) patients while no correlation is present in high-BMI (diabetic?) patients.
Key Proteins: GLUT4 (Insulin-dependent), GLUT1.
Sources: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41574-021-00471-8 | The integrative biology of type 2 diabetes. Nature 576, 51-60 (2019). | Metabolic messengers: adiponectin. Nat. Metab. 1, 334-339 (2019).
